body:
"I begin by observing that the accompanying terrorist issues are moot since
publication of  the Manifesto was in context to the Unabomber's promise -not-
to continue terrorist acts.  So the Manifesto must instead be read as a
 pacifist document and evaluated/assessed independently of terrorism."

------------------------------------

Ross made some good points on Jeff's assertion that the manifesto is a
"pacifist document". I would add that TK reserved the right to acts of sabotage
(which wouldn't involve killing). Is sabotage a pacifist activity?

But, consider the following passage. Paragraph 4: "We therefore advocate a
revolution against the industrial system. This revolution may or may not make
use of violence."

The manifesto may be considered many things. But, I would never think of
calling it a pacifist document.

-Susan
